population_banner:
POPULATION: this projection covers 48 declared ET-CC members and 29
declared in-population OC checks. That is the slice adjudicated so far,
and it is NOT the whole conformance picture: the full comparison is 281
ET-CC members and 173 in-denominator OC checks, of which 233 members and
130 checks are not_yet_adjudicated -- a third state, distinct from
bucket 1 -- owned by the tickets the crosswalk's own
`outside_the_population` block names. A further 14 checks carry an edge
without being declared by any file, so they are counted in neither.

A count of zero in this view means zero WITHIN THAT SLICE. It does not
mean zero in the suite. As the declared population grows this projection
re-runs and fills.

EVERY FIGURE ABOVE IS INTERPOLATED from the crosswalk being projected;
none is written here. The [population_statement] guard refuses a
population figure that is not.

rows.escalation: no_axis_contact — every axis of this check is silent. A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis is no match, not a partial one; generalised to 1 axes that is this edge. §3's table has no row for it, so it escalates rather than being bucketed.
rows.evidence: client_tool_schemas_test.exs:125-146. The member's `invalid_tool/1` helper (:55-63) builds exactly the fixture's `invalid_object_header` class — an `x-mcp-header` on a property of `"type" => "object"` — so the counterpart check is unambiguous. The single axis is SILENT: the check's subject is whether the client CALLED the tool, and this member deliberately calls it, asserting instead that the call carries no headers (`assert [] = … Keyword.get(:headers, [])`). The two are not in conflict — the call here is the TEST's choice through `Client.call_tool/3`, not the client's own selection — but the assertion's subject is the headers, not the calling.

rows.note: ALL AXES SILENT. Recorded and ESCALATED, never bucketed, per this file's all-silent rule. The question for the PM is narrow and worth asking: our client excludes the tool from tools/list and drops its annotations, but does not refuse a direct `call_tool/3` on the name. Whether SEP-2243's `MUST reject (exclude) such tools` reaches that far is a requirement reading, not an adjudication this file can make.

title: escalated — routed to the PM, in NO bucket
what_this_is: THE ELEVENTH VIEW, OUTSIDE THE TEN. The crosswalk's own rule is that "an escalation is NOT a bucket and is never counted as one" (match-relation.md §7). These rows are therefore visibly excluded by rule, each with its reason, rather than invisibly dropped — and rendering one into a bucket would launder a PM escalation into an adjudication, which is the one thing this ticket must not do. AC2's partition holds over the 52 BUCKETED edges; these 5 are enumerated here and are counted in the edge equation as their own term.
